geeklist.title: BGG.CON Virtual Flea Market 2022
geeklist.description:
[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b]Virtual Flea Market 2022[/b][/size][/COLOR] [size=14][COLOR=#FF0000][b]Tables have been assigned![/b][/COLOR][/size][/center]Final change in C-M! [imageid=7165521 medium] [b]Sellers tickets are now CLOSED. Badges will be strictly checked at the door by Team Geek.[/b]
[size=14][b]PLEASE READ THIS ENTIRE HEADER!! IN ORDER THAT THIS CHAOTIC EVENT WORKS FOR EVERYONE, IT'S IMPORTANT THAT YOU READ EVERYTHING![/b][/size]
[u][b]General[/b][/u] Here is the concept - For people who are travelling to the convention, sellers only want to bring games that they have sold. Buyers want to plan how much space they need to bring games home. Enter the Virtual Flea Market. If you have items that you'd like to sell at BGG.Con, list them here with the condition of your items, and the price or terms you'd like to sell for. Buyers settle on a price with the seller. At the con, buyers give an envelope with pre-counted money to the seller who hands them the game!
[center][COLOR=#009933][size=18][b]Special Updates for VFM 2022[/b][/size][/COLOR][/center] We want to thank Jeff Anderson and the BGG.CON team for continuing to have the VFM for 2022. Please thank him so that he knows that the effort towards making all this possible is appreciated. In order to continue to make this event possible, we really need every one to be polite and follow all the requirements below. [b]Coordination:[/b] I (Sterling Babcock, Solamar) will be running the Virtual Flea Market and attending. My wife, Marcia (RedPhoenixNia) will also be helping me as well as Team Geek.
[b] BGG.CON 2022 On Site Conditions:[/b] The VFM will be held in Reunion EFGH Thursday evening (6p-7p VFM Setup, 7p-8p VFM). There are three doorway entrances the bottom (of the eventual image). The three doors up the right-hand side (into Reunion D) can be used for exits but NO lines may form in Reunion D as it also serves as access to open gaming in Reunion ABC.
There are 80 tables, each one for an individual seller. Each seller will be limited to what they can store on and underneath a 6'x30" table. There will be NO sellers doubling up on a table, nor can one seller have more than one table to give as many as possible the opportunity to participate. Jeff is comfortable with no more than 400 people in this room at one time. [b]Please help in any way you can to be extremely polite and helpful![/b]
[b]We will follow the official BGG.CON 2022 policy on Masks:[/b] the official BGG.CON mask policy is now tied to the "low/medium/high" risk ratings on a county level as specified by the CDC: https://tabletop.events/conventions/bgg.con-2022/pages/health-safety-protocols It is possible we won't be requiring masks at the convention but simply recommending them, like we did at BGG.Spring: https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/297887/virtual-flea-market-delivery-bggspring-2022
[b]VFM Limits and Arrangements:[/b] We limit participation by having an event scheduled for "VFM Sellers" with 80 tickets available and another event for "VFM Buyers" with around 300 tickets available. Jeff plans to open up event scheduling sometime after September 20. Sellers: https://tabletop.events/conventions/bgg.con-2022/schedule/33 Buyers: https://tabletop.events/conventions/bgg.con-2022/schedule/34
To participate in the VFM meetup Thursday night as a seller you must have a ticket from the "Sellers" event. Ticketed sellers may only participate as buyers as well if they have arranged with the seller at the adjacent table to handle their transactions while they are away. They do not need a buyer ticket - the TTE system won't even let them get such a ticket as you cannot double-book yourself.
[b]There is no limit to participation on the VFM Geeklist[/b] but unless both the Seller and Buyer have tickets for the Thursday night meetup, the transaction will have to be arranged individually. We cannot directly monitor this, so we need your help! If you are a seller of just a few games, please mention that in your listing that you are doing personal meetup and please do not get one of the few seller tickets! If you are a large seller, please identify that you have an event ticket in your listing!
[size=18][b]Virtual Flea Market Main Information:[/b][/size] [size=12][b]VFM Delivery Meetup: Thurs 7 pm - 8 pm in Reunion EF. (Do NOT enter before 7 pm!! We need space to set up.)[/b][/size]
[u][b]Seller Guidelines[/b][/u] 1. Please do add your items - the more items, the more interest! How you sell your items is up to you! Fixed Price, Auction, Dutch Auction, it doesn't matter. Everyone is on their own - no one will be monitoring your items but you. Note: Sellers should comment or change the listing to show agreed upon sales, whereupon they are committed. 2. Mark sold items as: SOLD so that the summary tools can remove it from the available list. 3. Whatever you do, [b]PLEASE DON'T DELETE YOUR ITEMS[/b]. Mark them as sold or no longer available. With as many items as we get on the list, people rely on the entry numbers. Having them change with deletions makes it harder for everyone to pay attention to the items they are interested in. 4. There is an [b]easy way to add items[/b] to the geeklist, courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994): Alphabetical search tool: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/303285 The link to add games is: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/303285 5. Sellers will be allowed into the room to set up between 6-6:45pm on Thursday evening. No games will be allowed into the room after 6:45 pm - no unticketed sellers sneaking in as ticketed buyers (All tables will be already assigned). You may NOT use hotel luggage carts. Sellers stay on INSIDE of tables. Do NOT block the outside traffic with games! You are, of course, welcome to arrange other times/methods for your swaps on an individual basis (but see the note about a Tuesday meetup below). 6. You must remain at your assigned table until all your games are delivered. Please be kind, bring a sign, and try to help each other out. 7. Sellers should arrange a bulk commission at the BGG Marketplace (details to follow) 8. Sellers who only have one or two items should help by allowing official VFM meetup tickets go to people who need them. Please meet outside the VFM if you only have a few items! 9. Sellers MUST identify if they have an official meetup ticket and attend the WHOLE hour of the exchange until all your games are traded. (Some games may be traded earlier, but all your sales must be complete before you leave.) 10. Sellers who do NOT have an official meetup ticket or table should identify that so that buyers know that they have to make arrangements outside of the official VFM time! [b]11. If you are both buying and selling, you MUST bring a helper (or team-up with someone) to pick up your purchased games! If you still have items to deliver, you MUST be at your designated room location to deliver them.[/b] 11. Any attempt by a seller to deceive a buyer by significantly miss describing the item (e.g. missing stated expansion) will be dealt with harshly.
[b]Sellers: To keep the summary lists working, please update your items as follows[/b]: 1. When your item sells, please edit your items entry to include the word "[b]Sold[/b]" someplace. 2. If your item is an auction, please include the word "[b]Auction[/b]" someplace. 3. If you are selling an item that deserves an [b]alternate name[/b] in a summary list (i.e. Misc Game Accessory), please place this code in your item someplace: "+altname+ Whatever You'd Like To Call Your Item -altname-" 4. If you change your price, [u]please keep the new price on the same line of the geeklist[/u] (Do something like $25 $20) 5. Please [u]don't delete sold items[/u]!! Just leave them on the list. Thank you! 6. Per BGG Guidelines, it is the seller's responsibility to pay a small commission via a bulk item at the BGG Marketplace (Details to follow). If you go to YOUR item listing you will find: [b]Quick Marketplace Listing[/b] This is an easy way to get your listing made!
[u][b]Buyers Guidelines[/b][/u] 1. You may not enter before 7 pm because we require space to get many, many games setup for exchange, and large piles of games need to get into the room. PLEASE BE PROMPT at 7 pm!! We have to be clear of the room by no later than 8 pm to make room for other BGG events. Buyers stay on the OUTSIDE of the tables for ease of finding games. 2. Buyers MUST attend the START of the hour of exchange and stay until all your games are received. Do NOT be late and make people wait for you! Buyers are REQUIRED to either show up, or notify the Seller they will not be there. Do NOT be 'that guy' which makes a seller wait all hour trying to find you. You are to find the seller! 3. If you are a [b]buyer[/b], please bring one envelope for each seller you are buying from. [b]Each envelope should be marked on the outside with the seller's user name, and the items you are buying and should contain exact change[/b]. After doing this for a few years, we can tell you that this makes the event go much more smoothly for everyone. 4. The room will be organized according to Sellers' [b]User Names[/b]. If you are selling items, please know where your delivery location is. 5. Any attempt by a buyer to deceive the seller and pick up a game which you did not rightfully purchase will be dealt with harshly. Failure to follow these rules may cause you to be rejected from future Virtual Flea Markets.
[u][b]Room Plan[/b][/u] I will create a room plan so that there will be some semblance of organization to the [u]chaos[/u] that is the VFM. The room will be organized alphabetically by [b]Seller USER NAME[/b] (please note that the room will not be organized by first name, last name, or shoe size. It will be organized by the Seller's USER NAME). We will be putting signs on the tables so it is easy to see them. Please go to your table - it will make things a whole lot easier! Please stay tuned to this section, as we will update the room plan as we get closer to the event.
[u][b]Expectations[/b][/u] Since this event has gotten so large (also fun and successful), we need everyone's help to keep the event organized so we can continue it in future years. Please be on time. Please be considerate to the several hundred other people that are participating so this can continue to be a great experience! There is nothing more frustrating that walking through the room looking for someone, only to find out they are running late or wandering about the hall looking for their own pickups.
[u][b]Summary of Unsold Games[/b] - Use one of these links for an alphabetized list of games still available[/u] Despite not being a regular attendee, Steve Duff (UnknownParkerBrother) has put together a list based on code from Ron Parker (parkrrrr) that summarizes the games still unsold! Thanks Steve (and Ron)! Additionally, last year, John Munsch started working on new code for an improved summary list. He's made that available to us as well.
Alphabetical search tool courtesy of Eric Bettan (Carnage994: https://yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/303285
Links for 2022 not available yet. Hiding the 2019 links in spoiler.
[o][url=https://bgg.ucfhl.com/flea2019.cgi]2019 VFM Index[/url] (courtesy of Steve Duff (UnknownParkerBrother)) or [url=https://madgameslab.com/hammurabi.html?#/listings/261365]2019 Alternate VFM Index (courtesy of John Munsch)[/url][/o]
[u][b]Request List[/b][/u] If there is something you are looking for, think about adding it to Virtual Flea Market for Delivery to BGG.Con 2022 - Request List. [geeklist=304101][/geeklist]
[u][b]Shipping Suggestion[/u][/b] In the past, it is sometimes easy, convenient, and cost effective to mail a large box of items to the hotel ahead of the convention. The hotel will hold the box and delivered it to you when you arrive.
However, the hotel will likely be using its in-house FedEx service for handling incoming and outgoing boxes. FedEx will charge a per box handling fee for all incoming and outgoing boxes (plus an additional fee if you want the box delivered to your room). FedEx will also charge if you need to buy a box on the outbound side. For those of you travelling from afar, you should consider this alternative.
If you would like to mail a package to the hotel, you can mail the box to
Hyatt Regency Dallas 300 Reunion Boulevard, Dallas, Texas USA 75207
Then, mark the package with "Attn: [Your name and date of arrival]"
[u][b]Math Trade[/b][/u] While the VFM has become significantly larger in terms of number of items trading hands than the BGG.Con Math Trade, we continue to ask that people that participate in both be considerate of other participants. If you as a seller participate in both, please try to make sure that items are not listed in both at the same time. However, this will not be monitored. So if you do so, it is your responsibility to immediately mark items sold as no longer available in the Math trade, and mark them deleted from this list if they are traded. If you make a mistake and sell a game twice, it is your responsibility to fulfill all your commitments, no matter what the cost is to you. It is far better that you avoid conflicts like this.
[u][b]BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace[/b][/u] The BGG.CON Bazaar Marketplace is a separate event run at 10 am on Friday, where you can explore and purchase games at the con. It is not related to the Virtual Flea Market, but please do attend!
[u][b]Tuesday Night Meetup[/b][/u] In the past, some of the participants in the VFM have tried to set up a meetup on Tuesday night. BGG.Con staff has advised me that since they do not officially take any hotel space on Tuesday, there can be no official or unofficial events prior to Wednesday. So, please do not schedule such a meetup. All exchanges need to either take place in the Thursday event or arranged individually during the con.
Table Assignments are [b]not yet posted[/b]!
[u][b]More Tips accumulated from others:[/b][/u] [b]Sellers[/b]: A few tips or suggestions. 1. Create a spreadsheet with the games your selling. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Buyer Name, Buyer BGG Name, Comments, etc. If youâ€™re paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. 2. Send out geek mails and confirm with the game sale with people who have bought games from you. Sometimes people miss responses to game transactions. Run your sales through BGG Marketplace for BGG commission. 3. Have a full-length, printed sheet with your BGG User Name, Name, and Avatar/Logo on it for people to find you more easily. 4. Print out the table assignments beforehand. Circle your table. 5. Get there right at 6pm to set up your games and table. 6. You must attend the whole hour or until all your games being sold are picked up by Buyers. 7. Team up with a friend (or a few friends) if you are both Buying and Selling games. You cannot be both a Buyer and Seller at the VFM event. 8. Removable Sticky notes on the game with the name of the Buyer picking up your games would be helpful. 9. Please get your money out of the envelopes and deposit the empty envelopes in the trash. Please do not leave it for staff to clean up! 10. Remember it's the most wonderful game time (BGGCon!!) of the year! Be kind, courteous, and try to help others out as possible. This event is super fun!
[b]Buyers[/b]: A few more tips or suggestions. 1. Create a spreadsheet with the games you're buying. Create columns for Game Name, Game Cost, Method of Payment, Buyer Name, Buyer BGG Name, Comments, etc. If you're paying via PayPal, Venmo, etc. make a note. Print off your list prior to the event and bring it with you. 2. Buy plain envelopes. Write down the name of each game youâ€™re buying and the BGG name of the Seller. Provide exact change. Put your name on your envelopes so it's easily identified as paid by sellers or in case it gets lost. 3. Get there around 6:45pm and wait in line to get in. Buyers can't go in until 7pm. 4. Bring plenty of bags to haul off your 'new' games. You won't be able to use the luggage carts. 5. Possibly have a full-length, printed sheet with your BGG User Name, Name, and BGG Avatar/Logo on it for people to find you more easily. 6. Print out the table assignments beforehand. Circle or highlight the tables you need to visit. 7. Remember it's the most wonderful game time (BGGCon!!) of the year! Be kind, courteous, and try to help others out as possible. This event is super fun!

SInce I dont have a sellers ticket for the event, Do we just arrange to meet outside the VFM? what commonly happens?

[q="bakerid2000"]SInce I dont have a sellers ticket for the event, Do we just arrange to meet outside the VFM? what commonly happens?[/q] I'm hoping to be able to make most/all of my exchanges at the time of the VFM once I pick up everything from sellers who have tables. Otherwise, whatever you can arrange with your buyer. Some people make great effort to get games to their buyers. Others want their buyers to find them.

My suggestion: 1) geekmail everyone you sold to with your contact info (name/cell) then communicate via txt when you are available to exchange. 2) depending on how many games you cold you could let people know you will be outside of the event and do your transactions there. in the hallway infront of the room

[q="Larva_the_shinma"]My suggestion: 1) geekmail everyone you sold to with your contact info (name/cell) then communicate via txt when you are available to exchange. 2) depending on how many games you cold you could let people know you will be outside of the event and do your transactions there. in the hallway infront of the room[/q]
For buyers: - Please give out your cell number. I have had instances (few but still enough) where there was an expectation that the seller thought I should geekmail them only. - Make getting this game a priority during the day. If the seller has a meetup time that is reasonable. go to them and get your games. I know scheduling can be tough sometimes, but a lot of times it is a 5 minute trek to the person and back to get the stuff.
La Donn's suggestion is ideal for the situation. If you didn't want to do that, I have set up shop before on a table in one of the game rooms (table more in the corner) and just had the stuff with me and told people that I am there from time A to time B. Just camped out there and played games.

The one thing I would suggest avoiding when possible. Being a game mule for the times leading up to the VFM. For a few years I had people swinging past or asking me to meet them at x time at y location and i probably spent 6 hours running back and forth since i had so many games to sell/buy.

Personally I think we're all going to show up at the VFM with our games. Whether we have a table or not... We're going to be in the same area so even if we are meeting in the hallways, that's going to be a thing. Even if not on purpose ha.

It breaks item links (renumbering of the items is bad)

[q="ir1337"]It breaks item links (renumbering of the items is bad)[/q]
I believe if you actually link directly to the item it doesn't break the link. (See all the links in the list comments as examples.) Some people just write down item numbers instead of using the links, for whatever reason.

[q="repthrd"]I have never removed an item but just curious what is the issue with removing an item?[/q] It depends on how people keep records. If you wrote down, for example, that you have items 50-59, and an item prior to that is deleted, then the numbers "move up" and mess up your records.
If people bookmark the actual item URL that doesn't happen, because the back-end database ID that is assigned never changes. But many (most?) folks keep track of what pages their listings are on, or what item number (as opposed to database system ID) and then yes, if someone deletes an item it causes problems.
I like to use the item links myself, but I can't do that when I'm on my phone.

Question: For those of you who buy and sell and don't have a buddy to pick up your purchased games during the VFM; What is the best way to go about picking your games up?
Do sellers have the opportunity to go ahead and pick up their bought games games before (6-6:45) the VFM opens to the other buyers?

Usually yes, and the room isn't that huge where you can't step away for 1 minute to run to another table while the person next to you keeps an eye on your stuff. People know people and we will be like "oh that person is right over there."

#1 rule: don't be late! Most of the activity gets done in like 15-20 minutes, even though it's technically scheduled for an hour. Don't be that person that has a line waiting at their table and you show up at 7:30 or later.

[q="Munin"][size=18][u]How to Release a VFM Seller's Ticket[/u][/size] 1) Go to [url=https://tabletop.events/conventions/bgg.con-2022]BGG.CON 2022 on Tabletop.events[/url] 2) Login 3) Select your account name (in the upper right corner of the page) 4) Select My Receipts (under Conventions in the right side menu) 5) Select the receipt where you ordered your VFM Seller's Ticket 6) Select the red Delete button on the line of your VFM Seller's Ticket 7) Confirm deletion 8) Earn your angel wings [/q]

They're wanting to pull your table because we use automated tools to search a list with over 7,000 items in it, and the tools rely on you following the rules of the list in order for admin to know whether you actually need a table. I understand your frustration, but this is a self-inflicted wound.
If you don't keep your table, then it's up to you to complete your sales, table or no. I sold 100 games last year, without a table, between my own and what I was muling for others. You'll survive.

[q="seppo21"][q]11. If you are both buying and selling, you MUST bring a helper (or team-up with someone) to pick up your purchased games! If you still have items to deliver, you MUST be at your designated room location to deliver them.[/q] During the spring VFM, helpers were allowed to come in during set up. Is that going to be allowed in the fall? Also, once sellers arrive and get set-up, will they need to remain at their table until the buyers are allowed in at 7? [/q]Spring is a smaller con generally. Technically, the seller comes in at the seller time, and the helper comes in at the buyers time. We are trying to keep it organized so that the sellers can get things into the room and set up efficiently. We don't really want buyers wandering around and picking up games during setup. That being said, if you have a lot of games to sell and need help getting them into the room, message me and I will allow you to bring a helper in. Generally common sense takes the case. If you are doing something out of the ordinary, contact me, or be extremely courteous (e.g. if you are passing by someone, or are not interrupting them as they are ready, you might be able to trade with them.) Anything done with great courtesy that generally makes sense should be reasonable.
Which brings be to a personal side request (unrelated to this message): It seems to me that the world is having problems partially because people are being less considerate of each other. So if any of you all see someone doing something kind to others at the con, contact me and let me know. I want to find a way to reward those people, even if it is out of my own pocket.

A few comments: 1) The 1 seller per table, perfectly alphabetical system that was had last year was very efficient. It was clean, fast, and easy to get games. I liked it. 2) The chaos of previous years was fun but not efficient. It could take someone that bought a lot of games the entire hour to get their purchases.
So to me we have several options for the future that make sense. 1) Stick with the 80 tables for 1 seller per table. (and maybe make it the top 80 sellers) - The issue here is it may alienate some sellers and there will always be that person that sold just as many games at person 80 but doesn't get a table. 2) Increase the # of sellers at tables. People that sell more than say 30 games (random number, that could be upped to 40 or 50) get their own table. Then break down the remaining tables to try to get to the above # with the least number of people. So plan to have 30/40/50 games per table. No more than 3 sellers per table but ideally 2 sellers. Doing this would probably have 20-30 of the tables with single sellers. Leaving 50-60 tables with say 2 sellers. (Honestly 3 sellers per table can be problematic) This should accommodate the majority of sellers that sold more than 15 games. Honestly those that sold 10 or less, while a pain, its still easy enough to meet up outside of the VFM to exchange. I typically exchange 1/3-1/2 or so of my sales and purchases outside of the VFM with people swinging past my room or me swinging past their room to do an exchange.
Any way we look at it some sellers are going to get upset that they don't have a table and honesty not everyone needs a table.

item.objectname: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game
item.body:
SOLD
Includes over 1700 cards!!!
[-][b]$75[/b][/-]
This is for a big collection. With FFG's latest releases, this can be upgraded, but honestly, you'll have enough content in this box. Most expansions not played (some not opened/still in shrink)
Contains: *2 base sets *Khazad-Dum Expansion *Over Hill and Under Hill Expansion *The Road Darkens Expansion *The Treason of Saruman Expansion *Conflict at Carrock Adventure Pack *The Dead Marshes Adventure Pack *A Journey to Rhosgobel Adventure Pack *The Hills of Emyn Muil Adventure Pack *Return to Mirkwood Adventure Pack *The Redhorn Gate Adventure Pack *The Watcher in the Water Adventure Pack *Road to Rivendell Adventure Pack *Hunt for Gollum Adventure Pack *Escape from Dol Guldur Adventure Pack *The Long Dark Adventure Pack
whew!
All games in great condition unless otherwise noted. All prices can be negotiated after some time originally posted unless otherwise noted. All my comments are 50% snark unless otherwise noted. All your comments are appreciated unless otherwise noted.
item.comment: Wow! That is an amazing deal! My number 1 game.
You know, it's a great deal for gifting as well!

Might help if you correct your spellings. It's:

item.comment:
I'll buy this.
If you sweet talk me, I might also buy the other ('probably the best') Pax game.

First, sold!
Second, You should totally buy Pax Ren as well. I have a rolled-up vinyl map that I can include for it. But one of the real beauties of Pan Ren is it's emergent complexity from a fairly simple design. Every time I've played it, I've been gone from making simple choices to being overwhelmed with complex choices to an Aha moment when a path to victory emerges. This is in part due to the way the card market works where there are emergent victory conditions (plus you must pay attention to what your competitors are doings while trying to hide your own intentions.)
Third, you are a remarkable individual with great taste in games. Pax Ren would be lucky to have you.

Sweet talk succeeded! I've heard great things about Pax Ren and enjoy playing games multiple times to engage with different strategies.
I'll reach out to Pax Ren to see how it feels. Wish me luck! 🤞

[q="Katore"]If you sweet talk me, I might also buy the other ('probably the best') Pax game.[/q]
[q="boredbeyondbelief"]Third, you are a remarkable individual with great taste in games. Pax Ren would be lucky to have you.[/q]
I'm tempted to submit an offer on one of Eric's games just for the sweet talk.

[q="deitied"]I'm tempted to submit an offer on one of Eric's games just for the sweet talk.[/q]
Highly recommend! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Would solicit sweet talk again.

In Relic Runners, each player takes on the role of a character keen to exploit and acquire relics that have been unearthed in a long lost part of the jungle. Each would be archaeologist has a colorful past — retired university professor, former army captain, etc. — and wants to be the first to get their hands on the precious loot to earn the most victory points.

Excellent condition.
In Colony, each player constructs and upgrades buildings, while managing resources to grow their fledgling colony. In a clever twist, dice are used as resources, with each side/number representing a different resource. Some resources are stable, allowing them to be stored between turns, while others must be used right away. Buildings provide new capabilities, such as increased production, resource manipulation, and additional victory points. Using dice-as-resources facilitates a dynamic, ever-changing resources management mini-game while players work to earn victory points by adding building to their tableau on their way to victory.
[-]$20[/-] [b]SOLD[/b]

While Farmer Bob is away, the foxes have assembled to raid the chicken coop so they can steal chickens to cram into their bags and get them back home for cooking into delicious chicken dinner. It's a fox-eat-fox world out there.
Not only will the foxes need to watch out for Toby the farm dog guarding the chickens, they will need to steer clear of each other. No chicken is safe in the coop or in the bags.
Roll the dice, steal the chickens, avoid the dog, and cook up some tasty dinner in Winner Winner Chicken Dinner. All of this, while you try to outfox your closest fox friends as you race to see who will end up with the most cooked dinners and chickens in your bag.
$10

But in this dimension, moving ships will travel towards the nearest object, which is usually another ship, and when those objects are moving either forward or backward, reaching the warp gate isn't always easy. Time is running out to save your crew and your ship! In Bora Bora, players use dice to perform a variety of actions using careful insight and tactical planning. The heart of the game is its action resolution system in which 5-7 actions are available each round, the exact number depending on the number of players. Each player rolls three dice at the start of the round, then they take turns placing one die at a time on one action. Place a high number on an action, and you'll generally get a better version of that action: more places to build, more choices of people to take, better positioning on the temple track, and so on. Place a low number and you'll get a worse action – but you'll possibly block other players from taking the action at all as in order to take an action you must place a die on it with a lower number than any die already on the action.

Players must leave at least one disc behind when moving, so the board gradually fills up and movement opportunities become more and more scarce. The player occupying the most spaces at the end of the game wins!

FITS (Fill In The Spaces) is essentially a multi-player Tetris. Each player has an inclined board on which they place different polyominoes, with three, four, or five squares. The German player tries to figure out where the bomber is going, making sure to efficiently use the fuel to get as many hits on the bomber as possible.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Cosmic Colonies is an orbit-drafting game of building a home in the stars. Players must leverage their workers' unique abilities to gather resources and construct new buildings while cleverly expanding their colonies. Each round brings new opportunities — and new talent. Your old workers will blast off to other players, while their workers orbit around to join your team![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$15[/-] SOLD
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] New - [I]Players begin with a ship, and travel from planet to planet, hiring crew, purchasing ship upgrades, and picking up cargo to deliver (jobs) all in the form of cards. Some crew and cargo are illegal, and can be confiscated if your ship is boarded by an alliance vessel. Travelling from planet to planet requires turning over "full burn" cards, one for each space moved. Most do nothing, but you can also encounter an Alliance ship, have a breakdown, or even run into Reavers. Completing jobs gets you cash. First player to complete the story goals wins.[/I]
[B]BIN:[/B] $18 New in Shrink
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]In Foodies, players take on the role of managers in a food court. During the game, they will add new dishes to their menu, connecting the stars between different dishes. These recipes come from all over the world, granting different bonuses when added. What's more, players can hire chefs to work in their kitchens, including special, prestigious chefs who are the best in the business. In the end, the player who gains the most popularity will be declared the food master and win the game.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] New - [I]In Ghost Fightin' Treasure Hunters, a.k.a. Geister, Geister, Schatzsuchmeister!, four intrepid treasure hunters are on a quest, searching for precious hidden jewels, but the phantoms in this house do not give up their bounty easily. As their ghoulish numbers grow, the treasure hunters must work together to acquire all eight jewels and escape the house before it becomes fully haunted or else face their own gruesome demise.[/I]
[B]BIN:[/B] $25 [b]New in Shrink [/b] I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

item.objectname: Harry Potter: Hogwarts Battle – Defence Against the Dark Arts
item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]Harry Potter™ Hogwarts™ Battle Defence Against the Dark Arts is a competitive deck-building game for two players, inspired by Harry Potter Hogwarts Battle. In this fast-paced game, players take turns playing cards, taking actions and acquiring new cards to build a more powerful deck as their defensive skills improve. Stun your opponent three times to win![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10 2 player deck building game
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]In the drawing game Loony Quest, players study challenging level cards, then try to replicate the outline to meet targets and avoid obstacles on their tracing sheets. Once finished, players place their sheets on top of the level card to see whether the drawings line up with the targets they meant to hit — or avoid. Largely inspired by video games, Loony Quest players discover various worlds, play with 3D and 2D levels, run into loony monsters — Loonies — and big bosses, trigger special stages, collect bonuses, use penalties on opponents, and gather as many Xperience points as possible to win.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$10[/-] SOLD

item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] New - [I]It's a fine dining frenzy! In Menu Masters, you are a world-class chef, brimming with ideas for the greatest menus ever crafted, but the only way to become the Menu Master is to beat the other chefs to Market Street for the freshest, most delicious ingredients! You may choose to open a store to earn some money...or just grab your shopping basket and be the first in line at the market. It's the only way to get the best selection! But beware of the other chefs as they drive up demand and increase prices! Earn your stars in this deliciously fun race to gourmet supremacy, proving you are the greatest of menu masters![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $5

Stories from the morning news come back in the afternoon and evening, getting stranger and more tangled each time.[/I]
[B]BIN:[/B] [-]$5 New in Shrink[/-] Marked as Sold to remove duplicate

[B]Condition:[/B] New - [I]Outburst is a game of lists. Two teams take turns trying to guess as many of the 10 answers to a topic on the cards. Bonus points can be earned by guessing a Target Answer determined by a die roll. The first team to 60 points wins! The game mechanism is very similar to the long time TV game show Family Feud, and itself seems to be the basis for the Canadian game show Talk About, which also spawned its own home game by Pressman.[/I]

But in "SHOOTIN’ LADDERS: Frag Fest", you’ll more likely learn a lesson in ‘mortality’ and that everyone gets their just desserts. item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Welcome to Tiki Island, home to nine colorful carvings all competing to be the top Polynesian Idol! In the fast-paced game Tiki Topple, players try to maneuver your secret tikis to the top of the line by playing the right combination of action cards. Use a Tiki Up card to move a tiki ahead in line. Tiki Topple sends opponents' tikis tumbling to the back of the pack. But watch out for the sneaky Tiki Toast cards, which knock your tikis off the board! Score the most points and call yourself the Tiki Master.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$5[/-] SOLD
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]In Tonga Bonga each player pilots a ship around a little group of islands with the goal of visiting four of the five remote islands and returning to Tonga Bonga Bay. Winning the race does not win the game, however. In addition to the payoffs for visiting each island (lower the more players who have visited it before you), money is also made on each turn when you roll your three dice and assign them as movement points to your opponents' ships. The better "salary" offered, the more likely you are to attract the best dice rolls to your ships -- but then, you'll have spent more money. And most money is what wins at the end of the game. There is more than one balancing mechanism in play, with opportunities aplenty to hit the leader. It's a lighthearted dice fest, but with interesting decisions and no obvious best strategy.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$20[/-] SOLD
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

item.comment: Hi! Is this the "medium" or "very small" box version of this game?

There are three versions of this game. The first edition in 2004 was part of the "small box" Alea series (#5). The second edition in 2014 was in the "medium box" series (#11). The most recent version (2018) is in the "very small" box series (#5), and was called "Puerto Rico: Das Kartenspiel" in German but the English version is called "San Juan" and (really unhelpfully) has *exactly* the same cover image as the 2014 second edition / medium box version. I'm looking for the most recent version in the "very small" box series.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Introduced by the Moors, azulejos (originally white and blue ceramic tiles) were fully embraced by the Portuguese when their king Manuel I, on a visit to the Alhambra palace in Southern Spain, was mesmerized by the stunning beauty of the Moorish decorative tiles. The king, awestruck by the interior beauty of the Alhambra, immediately ordered that his own palace in Portugal be decorated with similar wall tiles. As a tile-laying artist, you have been challenged to embellish the walls of the Royal Palace of Evora.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$20[/-] SOLD
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

Each player becomes a famous Walking Dead character while taking on the roles of Leader, Savior, Survivor, or Loner.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $5
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Gather up a team of heroes in Fantahzee: Hordes & Heroes to defend the town, roll the combinations to activate their awesome abilities, and fight your way through the monsters to the bosses. Defeat three of the five bosses, then tally up your trophies from the day. Collect the most VP to win![/I]
[b]Comes with Expansion[/b]
[B]BIN:[/B] $18

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]n a wave of challenges and bluffs, players compete for control of the sea. Play your cards right and watch your stack of fish grow. But just when you think you're the big fish... a bigger fish comes along. Gobble up the most fish and you win![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $3
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]A worker-placement game for 2-5 players with an interesting bidding mechanic. In many other worker-placement games, if an opponent beats you to a spot, you're out of luck. Not so in Leonardo de Vinci. Here, you can bid more workers to jump ahead in line. And people at the back of the line, can still get something, but they have to pay more to get it. The competition for resources is very dynamic and fun.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Mage Wars Academy features gameplay similar to Mage Wars Arena (née Mage Wars) with two mages in head-to-head combat to see who will be victorious.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$7[/-] SOLD
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]It's a cool, windy day in autumn, some time around 30,000 years ago. For several hours now, a group of hunters have been following a herd of mammoths. Will they succeed? Will they actually be able to bring down one of these giant animals? Its meat would last the entire tribe for several weeks...[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $8
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Each round in Miaui, players choose one of the cards in their hand — and everyone starts the game with the same cards numbered 1-12 — to show how deep they dive in the hope of catching the best fish. All kinds of fish are served at the feast but beware the gooey jellyfish and the thieving seagulls.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $5
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Good - [I]With Monster Fluxx, Looney Labs returns to the monster theme first explored in Zombie Fluxx, but now the zombies are joined by vampires, skeletons, an angry mob of villagers, and even Bigfoot![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$5[/-] SOLD
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]The boxed versions of the game have a number of changes: Players have cards numbered 1-12 and a jaguar, which has special rules There are only ten perches, three of which have special rules The defending card is always revealed A game consists of four rounds[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $15
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]Five large wooden dinosaurs are moving towards trees and picking up one tree from each corner of the game board. All dinosaurs which get back to their starting square before the (neutral) T-Rex gets there is a winner. Dinosaurs are moved by a color die which determines the color of the next square they can move to.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$12[/-] SOLD to remove a double listing
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]ith the new hero-game "Quest" players experience exciting adventures at the gaming table, that unfold just like a cinematic tale.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $5
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]From the Atlas Games website: "The industrious yet short-sighted Seismic Asphalt & Paving Company -- located in the sleepy town of San Andreas, California -- has put you in charge of one of its many road crews. Your job is to build a network of roadways around San Andreas proper. But San Andreas is rather prone to earthquakes, which have a tendency to destroy the beautiful stretches of pavement you've been laying. After all the asphalt is put down, which road crew will end up connecting the most highway in between quakes?"[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] [-]$3[/-] SOLD
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] New - [I]More specifically, in Smugglers players form the "sacks" used for smuggling out of modeling clay and hide their contraband within. The sacks are then rolled down a 3D path, with a die roll determining which hole in the fence the player needs to try to squeeze through. The player whose bag fits through the hole and who has the largest sack now checks the smaller bags, possibly taking the contraband hidden within. Who will prove to be the best smuggler?[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $3
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

Original cards for 7th Continent "Second Edition" Base Box and *not* the full game.

https://the7thcontinent.seriouspoulp.com/en/replacement_cards/
Because of the huge number of cards, I haven't noticed any differences in the cards and it hasn't been an issue when playing the game. The cards themselves are in excellent condition, as the cards that received the most use were sleeved as per recommendation by the FAQ on the Serious Pulp website. Did you happen to check on the dice for this one?
I did not but am off tomorrow and will do so.

It is missing die. I think the way to play it is with an UNO deck. You'd use the cards that are on the blocks, shuffle, and then flip the cards to find out what block has to be removed. Which in a way, may be more fun 🙂
I was traveling all day yesterday and didn’t see this, so sorry! Ignore the GM I sent this morning. If you will take $3 I would like to buy it 😄 Thank you!

I'm gonna stay at $5 I did a little research and found this out which makes the game playable:
Later versions of the game eliminate the Uno Cube. As a result, when a player pulls a block and places it on the top of the tower, the color and number or symbol of that block determines what color or number or symbol of the block the next player should pull out. While the "Reverse" and "Draw Two" blocks serve the same purpose as their respective counterpart faces in the Uno Cube, the Skip blocks pass the play to the player next to the next player. When a Purple Wild block is pulled by a player, that player names the color of the block the next player should pull out.

item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]War Eternal is a standalone game compatible with the cooperative deck-building game Aeon's End. Players struggle to defend Gravehold from The Nameless and their hordes using unique abilities, powerful spells, and an all-new cast of dynamic characters. Featuring a number of innovative mechanisms, including a variable turn order system that simulates the chaos of an attack and deck management rules that require careful planning, War Eternal can be played alone or combined with other Aeon's End content for a game experience like no other.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $20 Cards are still in shrink
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]In CATAN (formerly The Settlers of Catan), players try to be the dominant force on the island of Catan by building settlements, cities, and roads. On each turn dice are rolled to determine what resources the island produces. Players build by spending resources (sheep, wheat, wood, brick and ore) that are depicted by these resource cards; each land type, with the exception of the unproductive desert, produces a specific resource: hills produce brick, forests produce wood, mountains produce ore, fields produce wheat, and pastures produce sheep.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $15
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]In each round of Dr. Microbe, you're presented with a challenge card that shows some combination of microbes and (possibly) a superbug. Each player has tweezers and a petri dish that's divided into three small sections and one large one. As soon as the card is revealed, players must race to place the microbes (and superbug, if present) in their petri dish. What's more, they must figure out which microbes (and possibly the superbug) to place in their petri dish based on this rule: The superbug must always be a different shape and color than the other three microbes in your dish! Whoever fills their dish with the proper items first claims the challenge card, and whoever first grabs five cards wins the game![/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $5
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]You lead a gang of 5 mice in a race for cheese. To move your mice, you throw special dice with green, red, and yellow faces. A green face lets you move a mouse forward; a red face makes you move backward, and a yellow face does nothing. You even have special powers to help you out. Get one of your mice to the cheese first, and it's yours. Simple, right? Not quite! Your opponents are not sitting still - they can move their mice (and yours!) and use their special powers to slow you down.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $12
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]In the cooperative, press-your-luck game Hotshots, crews of 1 to 4 players take on the roles of wildfire fighters — crew boss, spotter, swamper, and sawyer — with special abilities, then roll dice on burning terrain tiles to match the combinations shown on those tiles. The more faces they roll, the better they fight the fire. Players can choose to cut firebreaks, which protect tiles from embers blown by wind gusts, or push their luck to reduce flames and possibly even generate reward tokens. If players bust and fail to match at least three of the six symbols on the tile, the fire grows. Another option is to maneuver vehicles — air tanker, helicopter, and brush rig — to save the forest.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.
item.comment: Simple game, but I really enjoy this one.

item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Kaiju Crush is a light strategy game with limited grid movement, shared objectives, and intransitive combat on a modular board.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Created by Paul Randles, designer of Pirate's Cove, and developed by Mike Selinker and Bruno Faidutti, Key Largo transports players into the Florida Keys in 1899. As the new century dawns, players ply the thriving trade of finding treasures in shipwrecks around the island. Before a hurricane hits, players need to search the many shipwrecks and sell the lost treasures to the island denizens for as much cash as possible.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

[B]Condition:[/B] Like New - [I]Kharnage is a fast and fun fighting game in a med-fan world in which you are the warchief of the mighty humans, the strong (and alcoholic) dwarves, the amazing horde of goblins, or the ferocious orcs (and their giant!). Your goal in Kharnage is to take control of something strategically essential, astoundingly beautiful, and envy of all other nations: a hill. Yes, just a hill. Admittedly, it is a nice hill. It may have a very commanding view of the surroundings, or it may not. You won't know until you get up there! To do so, you're going to have to drive off the armies of the other players by simply causing as much mayhem and bloodshed as possible.[/I]
[B]BIN:[/B] $8 With Dark Rampage expansion
I will be at the VFM, but I am also available to meet outside of the event. Thanks.

item.comment: It's currently $12.64 on Amazon. Would you do $10?

[q="boredbeyondbelief"]It's currently $12.64 on Amazon. Would you do $10?[/q]
Hi Eric Yorkston (boredbeyondbelief), thank you for your offer to purchase Marvel United - English edition with Venom (instead of The Wasp) for $10, which was a Walmart exclusive. The version sold by Amazon for $12.64 comes with The Wasp instead of Venom, so this is not an apple-to-apple comparison. I've also recently updated my price-matching policy to not include Amazon for the following reasons:
1. More favorable work conditions in my warehouse (okay, my house) 2. I support small business instead of trying to destroy them. 3. I have played no role in developing facial recognition software that infringes on citizen's privacy. 4. I pay my fair share of federal income tax.
All that being said, I would sell this version of Marvel United to you for $15. Will that work for you?

Hey Jason,
This is a wonderful and moving response. And I am supportive of your working conditions and limited use of child labor. Unfortunately, when comparing Amazon versions to Walmart versions, we’re probably comparing rotten apples to moldy oranges. The Walmart exclusive actually decreases the product’s value, as I’ve boycotted Walmart since the mid-90’s ever since they a) ran the mom&pop record stores out of business then blacklisted artists that were critical of their gun policies (e.g. Sheryl Crow) and b) used illegal payoffs to build a superstore on the property of Teotihaucan in Mexico.
I know the money on a secondhand product goes to the reseller and not the original company, but to keep with our metaphor, it still seems like the fruit from a poisonous tree. This needs to be a teachable moment.
So I will counteroffer with either a $12.64 offer or a $10 offer with me donating an additional $5 to a charity of your choice.
(BTW, if I bought from Amazon, I would purchase through their Amazon Smile program with a percent of the proceeds going to St. Jude’s)

I'm going to pass on your offer.
What really bothers me about the initial offer isn't the amount. (I probably would have made a counter-offer, regardless, but I would have seriously considered letting Marvel United go for $10.) It's not that you pointed out a retailer offering the same title for less. (It might have been helpful to know that Amazon has a significantly lower price than I do for this title. I'm pretty sure they dropped their price since I first listed it.) It's that you chose to do so as a public comment directly under the game listing instead of pointing out the price difference to me privately via geekmail. By doing so, you implemented a strong-arm tactic, whether intentionally or not, of essentially saying "If you don't sell this game to me for my offer amount, not only will I go buy it from Amazon, but I have let everyone else know where they can buy it for less and ensured that no one will buy this game from you at your list price." But I guess that isn't your problem, it's mine.
And as I pointed out, the version I have listed for sale (with Venom instead of The Wasp) is a different version than the one Amazon is selling (with The Wasp instead of Venom).

Hey Jason,
My sincerest apologies. I didn’t mean to offend nor break any norms when providing external pricing information.
I operate under the general assumption that individuals are trying to make an exchange at fair market value. I often see comments from sellers with comments along the lines of “pricing is hard, please help me if my price is out of line.” We often see buyers publicly providing bids with accompanied with comments like “how about $X, that is what the last copy sold for in the VFM.” Sellers counter with the price they purchased it for or the price it is currently selling for through other channels. I think in both these situations, people are providing the information not to strong-arm their negotiating partner, but to educate in the hope of reaching an equitable sale.
That said, I try not to kibbutz and provide market information when I am a passive observer to an offering that I am not a potential purchaser. For example, I didn’t (and won’t) post this price on offerings of this game in the VFM.
Again, I hope there are no hard feelings. I will make sure not to transgress like this in the future. And if you wish, I will delete my comments on your geeklist item.

Hey Eric,
I didn't think you had any ill intent and I understand you were trying to be helpful. We just have different school's of thought when discussing external pricing.
I have seen the comments you are referring to. I saw similar comments last year, made a comment at the bottom of the geeklist (not in relation to any one item) and the VFM blew up that day with people taking sides and offering opinions on this very topic. So this year, I wanted to avoid creating any controversy and have held my tongue when the seeing the same comments, until now because the comment was made on an item I have listed.
I don't think either of us needs to make any further comment on this topic but I will leave you with what Sterling had to contribute to the topic last year:
[q][b]Let's try to be as kind as we can to each other.[/b]
If you see an item that you yourself are interested in, and you you feel that you want to negotiate on the price: * Contact the person directly via geekmail. * Ask questions - Is the game in shrinkwrap? Does it have upgraded storage (some inserts can be $50!)? Does it have sleeved cards (which adds cost)? Does it have upgraded components? Does it have optional components? What is the condition? What language is it in? Do you have translations? Player Aids? * Perhaps make a counter offer on price politely * If you get these answers and still feel the item is not in your price range, just let it go.
Bottom line: Once you have an accurate representation of the details of what is offered, if you are reasonably close, perhaps negotiate. If you are not close, just let it go. There is no reason to fight it.
Finally: Comparing different offers from different people invokes a lot of ambiguity and should be avoided. Conditions of items and extras cannot be easily compared. There is also a nebulous factor of willingness to sell. There is a far cry from "I can let it go if I get a reasonable offer" vs "I need shelf space now, and anything will do!" Also note that sometimes games are offered at a major deal and an early buyer gets lucky ("Oh! I would have paid double for that! What a deal!"). That does not mean that all copies of that game should sell for that low price.
[b]I appreciate everyone working together to make this event fun for all.[/b][/q]

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]Lemonade Stand is played over seven turns (days), and each turn players start by turning over a forecast card which shows the weather forecast for the day along with number of customers and the price they will be willing to pay for each possible weather outcome. Players then place a 5, 10 or 15 cent price card down along with any signs or lemonade inventory they want to put out, all face down. All players reveal their cards at the same time and then a new forecast card is revealed which has an arrow pointing to one of five spots on the old forecast card, which determines which weather event occurred. Each player then collects money based on their price and # of glasses of lemonade invested versus the actual weather that happened.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $3

item.body:
[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]Spewed out amidst the rest of the 'Phantom Menace' merchandise, this little card game from Hasbro actually rises to a decent level for the true Gamer. item.comment: Unsolicited plug: This is a fun and somewhat unique game! Players bid for turn order, place lily pads, and move them around with the wind. Score points by getting lily pads in certain configurations. And you get to croak like a frog. 🙂 It's a two-player game that plays out in several rounds. And it looks good. Lance, I already have a copy of the game so I'm not really in the market, but if you wanted to let it go for $5 I would buy it, maybe to gift it later.

I don't have a complete inventory of all items, but it will contain AT LEAST the starter set and the expansions necessary for the following ships:
[u][b]Federation[/b][/u] Intrepid Class * U.S.S. Voyager Galaxy Class * U.S.S. Enterprise D Nova Class * U.S.S. Equinox Excelsior * U.S.S. Excelsior Sovereign Class * U.S.S. Enterprise-E
[b][u]Klingon [/u][/b] D7 Class * I.K.S. Gr'oth Var'Cha Class * I.K.S. Maht-H'A Negh'Var Class * I.K.S. Negh'Var K'Vort Class * I.K.S. Koraga K'T'Inga Class * I.K.S. Kronos One Raptor Class * I.K.S. Somraw
[u][b]Dominion[/b][/u] Jem'Hadar Battleship * 2nd Division Battleship * 4th Division Battleship Jem'Hadar Battle Cruiser * 2nd Division Battle Cruiser * 3rd Division Battle Cruiser Jem'Hadar Attack Ship * 3rd Wing Attack Ship * 2nd Wing Patrol Ship * 4th Wing Patrol Ship * 5th Wing Patrol Ship * 6th Wing Patrol Ship Cardassian Galor Class * Kraxon * Reklar Cardassian Keldon Class * Koranak Hideki Attack Fighters * 1st Wave Attack Fighters * Generic fighters * Generic fighters (2nd copy) Breen Battle Cruiser *Gor Portas
[u][b]Romulan[/b][/u] D7 Class * I.R.W. Algeron Romulan Scout Vessel * R.I.S. Vo Romulan Bird-of-Prey * I.R.W. Gal Gath'thong * I.R.W. Vorta Vor * I.R.W. Preatus D'Deridex Class * I.R.W. item.comment:
I just had a flashback...... [b] [i]Excerpt from the Diary of Chad Thriftington III[/i]
Nov 4, 1971[/b]
I had just returned from the United Kingdom where I had successfully helped foil a plan to sabotage the launch of the Prospero X-3. The trail had led to a gang of Chinese thugs hiding in the Congo, but when I stormed their hideout, all I discovered was a cryptic note stating they were responsible for the intimely death of Shamu a few months earlier.
I had stepped out of the shower, having washed the Congonese dirt from my chest hair, when the phone rang. It was Tonya! What was SHE doing back in town? I hadn't seen that blonde bombshell since she had saved Hubert Humphries life by pulling that sport coat full of dynamite off of him and then jumping into the Illinois & Michigan canal back in '68. Everyone; the FBI, The Illinois National Guard, the Cook County Police, myself, Mama Cass Elliot, EVERYONE, thought she was dead.
But here she was, alive, and back in love with me...or WAS she? She said she was only a few minutes away from my apartment and could she come by and catch up on old times. That was an understatement. I told her to come on by. I disabled the laser defense system and contacted my squad of ninja bodyguards, telling them to allow a blonde goddess to come on up to my place.
I dashed about the house, throwing on an old jacket and slacks when I heard the door open. It was Tonya, lovely as ever. I offered her a chair but she declined, muttering something about a phobia she had developed about chairs and how it causes flashbacks to a previous life in Atlantis.
She said she had something to show me (I grinned inwardly) and she pulled out a box of cubes with words on them. The box slid out of her hands and burst open upon the orange carpet. As we knelt down to gather the cubes I couldn't help but notice her hair, her eyes, her [-]cleavage[/-] dress.
Then, I realized that I hadn't placed the ninja squad back on alert, for at that very moment we heard the report of a rifle, the window shattered and the bullet stru...
[i][b] End of Excerpt from the Diary of Chad Thriftington III [/b][/i]

Exchange notes: :arrowE: I am planning to attend BGG Fall but will not have a seller table at the VFM. I can deliver to your table (if you are registered as a seller) or make other arrangements to meet during the convention. :arrowE: I accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. I also accept Venmo or Cash. :arrowE: I use [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/Condition_of_a_game]this article[/url] for determining the condition of the items I have for sale.
+sold+

item.body:
[-][b]This game came from the estate of a deceased friend; I was asked to dispose of his games. I don't have a history of the games beyond what I note below, except that as far as I know, he never smoked and my fairly sensitive nose has not detected the smell of smoke.[/b]
English edition (1992) Publisher: Milton Bradley [BGCOLOR=#FFFF00] Very good condition. Complete with extra parts! [b]The extra parts are a second electronic module and an extra set of plastic play pieces! Both electronic modules have been tested and work. [/b][/BGCOLOR]Apparently he get ahold of spare parts at one point. There is a fresh set of Duracell AA batteries in one unit.
Below are photographs of the actual game being sold.

The play board, just a bit of edge damage: [imageid=7128776]

Another view of the plastic pieces (again, original plus spares): [imageid=7128781]
The flattened side boards and plastic supports: [imageid=7128788]
The logsheet pads, the rule book and the assembly instructions (the rule book looks nearly new while the assembly instructions are somewhat wrinkled): [imageid=7128790]
The box is bowed and worn but still intact with, as far as I can tell, no repairs: [imageid=7128791][imageid=7128792]
Everything going into the box: [imageid=7128794]

I absolutely adore this game. So much so that I ended up with a second copy that I intended to give as a gift.
I have a full set of everything Obsession, new and in shrink. These are only available from the publisher. I'm not desperate to sell, at the same time I'm not looking to profit on the scarcity of this item.
The listed prices on the website are:
[thing=231733]Obsession base game[/thing]: 64 [thing=279067]Upstairs, Downstairs expansion[/thing]: 35 [thing=245392]Wessex Expansion[/thing]: 19 [thing=306634]Promotional Improvement tiles[/thing]: 12 Shipping to TX is: 24
[-]So the grand total if you bought from the website is $154
I'd probably sell this for $130?
Anyway, feel free to look at this and if you're interested comment below or reach out to me. Please note, I'll entertain offers between $100 and $154 (I won't sell it for more than it's worth, and I may not sell it below $130.) [/-]
And who knows, maybe no one wants this in the first place!
item.comment: Fantastic game. Definitely worth a look.
I'll make a starting offer of $100

[-]I'll offer $105 for Obesssion... I hear once you play this game... You become obsessed. :)[/-]
Outbid :(
It's true. The game has a cult-like following - me included! Plus, Dan Halligan is one of the most responsive and involved designers I've encountered.
I can't take it anymore, I'm...offering $135...out of pure...unadulterated...Obsession.

It is a fever from which I will never recover. All heat and hunger, which inflamed my senses.
$150 so I may once more FEEL SOMETHING so utterly brilliant, in the sullen world of longing where I henceforth subsist, bereft of joy, gray and dour. [youtube=W0p-pOf4KB8]

Though I am very tempted to bid $150.01 just to keep this going.....I bow to you sir. 😭
But I leave you with this earworm. The most 80's thing that has ever 80's. Like a butterfly. A wild butterfly. It will collect you and capture you.
[youtube=hIs5StN8J-0]
Sold to donovan. Thanks for the walk down memory lane and the sheer nonsense of almost all things 80s. Oh - and now I have an earworm.

These were from a board game cafe I used to own.
Each frame has a removable side so the plexiglass can be removed easily for cleaning or if you wanted to rework these to hold your own favorite game.
Islebound 46.5"x37" 3.5" deep $40 Machi Koro 44"x33.5" 1.5" deep $20 [-]Mahjong 25"x25" 2.5" deep $10[/-] Claimed by Eric Galatune 31"x31" 1.5" deep $10 [-]America! 27.5"x27.5" 1.5" deep $10[/-] Claimed by Eric [-]Kingdomino 28.5"x33.5" 2.5" deep $20[/-] Claimed by Benjamin [-]The Game of Life 33.5"x39.5" 2.5" deep $20[/-] Claimed by Donovan [-]Wits and Wagers 27.5"x39.5" 2.5" deep $10[/-] Claimed by Eric [-]Karuba 26.5"x37.5" 2.5" deep $20[/-] Claimed by Donovan
The frames are heavy
If you're looking for a nice piece of art for your board game room look no further.
Will be at the con Tue-Sun.
Friday, November 4th @ 3pm is the cut off for my items so I can get them packed up.

item.objectname: Time of Legends: Joan of Arc
item.body:
Are you looking for a new lifestyle game? Then have I got a game for you!
Time of Legends: Joan of Arc! Kickstarter Mega Bundle
This is a metric ton of minis and content. Please see photos.
Contents: Maiden Pledge: aka Base Game and Reliquary Box of Stretch Goals Unleash Hell Box Legendary Dragon (This "Mini" is awesome!) Cravant Expansion scenario Hard Back Scenario Collection Book NIS New 1.5 Rulebook Deluxe Storage Box full of Gametrayz goodness Banners and Bases
Everything is condensed to the Deluxe Storage Box, Reliquary Box, and Unleash Hell Box. Except the Dragon... because he's huge.
Also a ton of custom 3D Printed unit holders to keep everything nice and neat.
Some of the models have been sticky-tacked to their bases as seen in the photos.
Cards components are in very good condition, some cards still in shrink, appears mostly unplayed.
Looking for $350 on this lot.
Will be at the con Tue-Sun.
Friday, November 4th @ 3pm is the cut off for my items so I can get them packed up.

Weapons and Warriors Bundle

Condition: Used Price: $60
-Box is in good shape given it was made in 93. -Everything is combined into the Castle Siege Box -Castle Siege Set is about 80% complete. It is missing a variety of pieces (the 5 knights on horses, two tents, a cannon, 6 red and 6 blue soldiers, one tree, and some cannonballs though there are plenty of them left) -Despite what is missing, game has plenty of pieces to play with. Each side has their own castle and smaller fortress and enough soldiers to fill them. Each side has two catapults and a crossbow. You will have to share the cannon. -Rubber bands have been replaced so everything still works -There are a lot of bits (over 200) so if you have any questions please let me know.

item.objectname: Legendary: A Marvel Deck Building Game
item.body:
[size=18][b]$400[/b][/size]
Large collection of [thing=129437]Legendary[/thing]. All cards are sleeved (except extras that aren't required--duplicates of base game cards that came in the Marvel Studios Phase I expansion--and the schemes since you only use one per game and they don't need to be shuffled. All cards are in excellent condition.
All cards are stored in a 5 column card storage box as pictured. It is heavy, probably around 30-35 pounds. Includes cardstock printed dividers as pictured with space for more cards or the playmats as shown.
[ImageID=7135905 inline] [ImageID=7135908 inline] Full box and zoomed for detail on dividers.
Includes the following sets in addition to the base game's 500 cards:
[b]Standalone expansions[/b] Large sets of heroes and villains with masterminds and schemes in addition to required starting decks. Each comes with a playmat to use as an alternative to the base game's board. [thing=156689][/thing] (500 cards) [thing=252985][/thing] (400 cards)
[ImageID=7135906] [b]Big box expansions[/b] Many heroes, villains, masterminds, and schemes. About 350-400 cards each. [thing=223362][/thing] [thing=193513][/thing] [thing=137762][/thing] [thing=248084][/thing]
[b]Small box expansions[/b] Five heroes, a few villains, two masterminds and associated schemes. About 100 cards each. [thing=255616][/thing] [thing=186845][/thing] [thing=200983][/thing] [thing=239469][/thing] [thing=231037][/thing] [thing=142020][/thing] [thing=163106][/thing] [thing=149922][/thing]
That's about 3600 cards if my math is right.
In addition, I still have all original boxes stored in a closet if you are interested in acquiring those as well. They take up a lot of space, but you wouldn't be interested in this collection anyway without being local to the con or with a large transport vehicle.
[imageid=7135911 inline] [ImageID=7135907 inline]

[size=18][b]$30[/b][/size][/-]

Item: Custom Printed Stone Age Play Mat Condition: New Price: $25 but willing to accept offers
Description I used some art found in the Stone Age gallery to create a custom play mat. It was not until after I printed the image and reviewed it that I realized the creator had changed two items compared to the base game. I got those corrected and created a new mat, leaving me with the first printing I made with two "errors." If you play Stone Age without the "Style is the Goal" expansion, then the mat is fine.
Here is the full playmat image [ImageID=7148145 medium]
On my first attempt I left the border white. In the image below you can see the original printing and the corrected printing to compare what the changes are. [ImageID=7148141 medium]
In the Style is the Goal expansion you can advance on the jewelry track. As you advance, you can swap tusks for other resources. In the version I am selling there is a 2:2 section added in the middle which provides additional value / incentive to trade. You could ignore this, or play by this modified rule.
Also in the Style is the Goal expansion there are now five civilization cards to select from. The first four are purchased as normal. The fifth card can only be paid for with tusks. The cost is supposed to be three tusks for the card, plus an additional three tusks for a hidden card. On the playmat you can see the cost is represented as four, not three, for the first card.
If you purchase this item I will not collect payment until you have had the chance to inspect it in person. I printed this via Inked Gaming and my cost was around $50. The overall mat size as printed is 28" by 24". The play area is sized exactly to fit the game components, so the huts and cards and everything else fits just as it would on the game board. I just like playmats better. :)
Exchange notes: :arrowE: I am planning to attend BGG Fall but will not have a seller table at the VFM. I can deliver to your table (if you are registered as a seller) or make other arrangements to meet during the convention. :arrowE: I accept PayPal Friends and Family once you have had the opportunity to inspect your purchase. I also accept Venmo or Cash.
+altname+ Stone Age Custom Printed Playmat -altname-

item.body:
[size=18][b]AT-43 Initiation Set: Operation Damocles[/b][/size]
[b]Rackham[/b]
This has been sitting at the back of a set of shelves for years. If I recall, it was a purchase at the very first BGG.con charity auction. I am very much wanting for this to find a new home where it will be loved. The description below is from the last time I had it listed in a VFM, sometime pre-COVID.
The box is a little banged up but is still intact. Contents in general are in excellent condition. However, a lot of items are held in place by plastic tabs in the insert which has caused some minor indentations. One of the mechs seems a little fragile. One arm has broken off and another piece is very loosely attached (and will likely come off soon). I think a little glue would fix both of these. One of the legs seems a little loose as well but is in no danger of falling off. Everything is present. Previously BGG.con library copy so has a barcode sticker from library on back.
